acceptance: A scope that runs on an expired context reports the deadline, not only 'produced no execution results' (red today)
The budget semantics (per scope or shared) are pinned by a test

consumed.resolution: The Go lane budget is pinned as one deadline shared by every scope (laneBudget, TestRun_TheGoLaneBudgetIsOneDeadlineSharedByEveryScope); a scope that finds it spent is reported 'budget ... was spent before this scope started' and never started, and a scope that failed carries its exec error plus 'expired while this scope ran: context deadline exceeded' (go/internal/acssuite/acssuite.go).

fix: Include execErr in the no-results error. Decide the budget explicitly: either a per-scope deadline, or a shared deadline whose exhaustion is reported as such ('the go lane's 600 s budget was spent before scope X ran'), never as a predicate package that produced nothing.
summary: Cycle 1762's second audit failed with 'acssuite: active predicate scope "./acs/regression/apicover" produced no execution results'. runGoTest runs every scope under ONE context whose deadline is gc.acs go_timeout_s (600 s) for all scopes together; under the load above, the cycle's own scope (a -count=50 -race predicate) spent the budget, so the next scope's `go list` died on the expired context. The len(results)==0 branch returns without execErr, so the cause (context deadline exceeded) never reached the report.
title: The host predicate run reports 'produced no execution results' and drops the error that explains it
